campaigns.title: This Guru Purnima, help IITian Bipin ensure tribal kids of Majuli island get free education
campaigns.description: “The Hummingbird School is my only hope to succeed in life. I feel I am trying to swim out of this place (Majuli) and my school stands as a beacon on the other side of the river. If my school closes down, I feel I will drown in this river. Not just me but every child in villages around here and our families depend on this school”, says Roopjyoti, a bright, young student of Ayang Trust’s The Hummingbird School.Majuli Island, where The Hummingbird School is situated, faces severe floods and constant riverbank erosion, leaving most of its residents struggling to survive. For the children of this impoverished tribal community, education remains their only path to hope and dignity.Your support to Ayang Trust’s Hummingbird School can ensure that its students can have a future different from their parents who are struggling to get even two meals a day. Donate now.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).From IIT Kharagpur to Majuli“When I first visited the remote villages of Majuli I was shocked. The extent of the struggles here was beyond my imagination. These villages had no connectivity to the outside world, and very limited access to healthcare and quality education”, says Bipin Dhane, founder of the school. Bipin, who grew up in the small town of Satara in Maharashtra, faced countless financial hardships. Despite his struggles, Bipin secured admission to the prestigious Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, and then went on to take up a job in Singapore. Owing to his childhood experiences Bipin was always inclined towards helping the less fortunate, and he believed in the transformative power of education. It was in 2016 that Bipin left his lucrative career abroad and moved to Majuli, to provide the children from this inaccessible river island education they were deprived of.“Whatever little money I had saved, I gave it to my parents. I had no money to start the school. It was then that villagers came together to build bamboo huts. Each family donated bamboo, wood, and whatever little they could. It was the parents of our students who erected huts for the school to start”, shares Bipin while talking about the inception of The Hummingbird School in 2017.Help Bipin save underprivileged children of Majuli Island from generational poverty and give them a chance to succeed. Donate now.Donate to save future generations“People of the island value education greatly because they know that their children have no future without it. Parents have vested their faith in The Humming Bird School because they don't want their children to suffer the way they have been”, says Bipin. Bipin says, “Today we have over 300 students in our school and about 90 children live in our hostel. Many of these children are orphaned or come from single-parent households, struggling each day without adequate care or resources.. I urge each one of you to come forward and donate to us so we can help hundreds of children escape from the cycle of poverty and build lives of dignity, hope, and opportunity.”Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s largest and most trusted online donation platform, to help children of Majuli Island get an education and break the cycle of poverty.

campaigns.title: Help Mangaltai give 150 abandoned HIV+ orphans life-saving care, education and a loving home
campaigns.description: “During a visit to a nearby village, I found two abandoned babies left to die in a cowshed. Visibly fragile and covered in dirt, the condition of the little ones left me in shock. Moved by the sight, I inquired in the area and was told that these babies were left there by their own family after they were diagnosed with HIV. I immediately brought the babies back home. This was in 2001 and that marked the beginning of a two-decade-long struggle to save abandoned HIV+ children from dying on the streets,” says 75-year-old Mangal Shah, fondly addressed as tai by her 150 adopted grandchildren. Mangaltai founded Palawi with a mission to give abandoned HIV+ children a second chance at life and, more importantly, to right the wrongs that society had done to them. For over two decades, she has rescued hundreds of children off the streets and given them the love they were denied for no fault of theirs. She has given the children life-saving medical care and education while helping them lead normal lives.“It does not cost us money to give them the love they deserve, but the cost of medical care, food, shelter, and education is more than what I can shoulder on my own and I need urgent help,” pleads Mangaltai. Help 70-year-old Mangaltai save the lives of her 150 HIV+ grandchildren. Donate now. Every child deserves a futureHailing from the predominantly rural area of Pandharpur in Maharashtra, Mangaltai faced countless challenges and opposition from people in the area. “I was often told that these children are HIV+ and they are not going to survive long. What is the point of wasting money, time and effort behind them,” recalls Mangaltai. “But I told everyone I am not going to give up on any of these children. Every child deserves love and care. Every child deserves to have a chance at a future,” she adds. Narrating a story about a 5-year-old boy Mangaltai says, “We rescued 5-year-old Pranay (name changed) from a nearby village in 2005. He was severely malnourished, sick and had a gaping wound on his head. Seeing the baby’s condition and the maggot-infested wound, doctors gave him six months to live. But Pranay is now 22 years old, he is financially independent and leading a normal life with dignity. What would have happened if I gave up on him?” Mangaltai has faced severe discrimination all along her journey with Palawi, owing to her work and for standing up for the rights of HIV+ kids. She was driven out of schools when she tried to get admissions for her children. “The discrimination against our children was such that they were not even allowed to set foot in any of the schools in this area. We were left with no choice but to start a school of our own,” says Mangaltai.The healing power of loveAccording to Mangaltai, the love that children of Palawi receive is one of the strongest factors in their recovery and healthy childhood. “We are there for these kids throughout the day. These kids have low immunity and are prone to illness. Which is why we need to be extremely cautious. We need to have regular health check-ups to ensure they are safe and healthy. But all of this comes at a cost. A cost that I alone can not take care of,” Mangaltai says. Help Mangaltai change the lives of hundreds of abandoned HIV+ orphans and give them a loving home, medical care and education, so they too can live fulfilling lives in future. Donate now.

campaigns.title: Help visually impaired Shivaprakash give 40 blind girls shelter, education and care
campaigns.description: At the age of 8, Shivaprakash lost his vision. But what could have become a life of despair became something else entirely. Shivaprakash went on to complete his Master’s degree and eventually founded the Divya Jyothi Charitable Trust, an organisation born out of personal struggle and driven by a powerful mission, to educate and empower blind girls, who are among the most neglected and marginalised in society.In many families, blind daughters are hidden away, seen as a burden, and in some cases, even as a curse. They are denied the right to dream, grow, or be independent. At Divya Jyothi, Shivaprakash is changing that narrative. Your support can ensure that no blind girl is left behind simply because of her disability. Donate today to help them stand tall, proud, and self-reliant. Donate nowDonate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).Education is survivalIn communities where gender and disability intersect, blind girls face deep-rooted prejudice and extreme isolation. Many are denied even basic schooling and are left dependent on family members for the rest of their lives. Recognising this, Divya Jyothi began with a simple yet radical step: to provide blind girls with computer training so they could access the digital world and open doors to employment.But the journey didn’t stop there. The NGO went on to launch a braille transcription centre, ensuring girls have access to learning materials that suit their needs. As Shivaprakash says, “Without education, no one can do anything. That's why education is even more important for blind girls.” Education isn’t just about literacy, it’s about self-worth, decision-making, mobility, and freedom. It’s about giving these girls the same right to participate in society that sighted individuals often take for granted.From rejection to respectIn a country where blind girls are often treated as liabilities, Divya Jyothi is rewriting their futures. Over 1,000 girls have graduated from the Trust’s training centres. Many of them come from families that had almost given up on them. Today, these same girls are government employees, corporate professionals, and role models in their communities.More than 200 graduates have secured jobs in the public sector. Over 300 are now employed in private companies. Every success story is proof that with the right support, blind girls don’t just survive, they thrive. “Most girls are neglected by their families. This is a major challenge for them,” says Shivaprakash. By providing them with skills and confidence, Divya Jyothi is turning neglect into empowerment and helplessness into hope.Donate to help 40 blind girls find independenceAlmost 40 girls are currently enrolled and will directly benefit from your support. These are girls with potential, courage, and ambition—but they lack the resources to pursue an independent life. “I request each one to come forward and donate to help blind girls lead independent lives in society,” urges Shivaprakash.Help Divya Jyothi Charitable Trust break the cycle of neglect. Your donation can give a blind girl her first lesson, her first job, and a life of dignity.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Divya Jyothi Charitable Trust in its mission to shelter and educate neglected and abandoned blind girls.

campaigns.title: Help Mansi bring hope into lives of children fighting for life, Donate now
campaigns.description: When even hospitals and doctors gave up on children fighting for life Mansi Shah stood by them. Mansi founded Happy Feet Home, an NGO that cares for children fighting severe illnesses like thalassemia, HIV, Cancer, etc. Despite being discouraged repeatedly, she refused to turn away from children who were often overlooked simply because their journeys were difficult and uncertain. Today, Happy Feet Home provides children with medical care, nutritious food, education, emotional support and, above all, the love and dignity every child deserves.Your donation can help ensure these children continue receiving lifelong care. Donate today and give them the chance to live with hope.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking.Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).Born from one unforgettable momentHappy Feet Home was born from an experience Mansi could never forget. "I was very attached to this 3-year-old girl. She had a brain tumour," she says. When the child hugged her tightly before boarding a train home, it felt like a final goodbye. That heartbreaking moment inspired Mansi to dedicate her life to children who may never receive a cure. "If I start something, I will work with children who have illnesses which may not have a cure... That's when the idea of Happy Feet Home came into my mind."Every donation changes a child's futureMany children arrive at Happy Feet Home carrying far more than an illness. "It's not 1, not 2, but 3 or 4 issues that they are grappling with in life," Mansi explains. Poverty, abandonment and years without affection often leave emotional scars as deep as their medical conditions. Some children have even told her that the first hug they ever received was after arriving at the centre.Yet with proper nutrition, medicines, counselling and constant care, lives begin to change. One girl who was once not responding to treatment is now a healthy college student. Another boy arrived weighing just 17 kilos after living on the streets. Today, he is healthy and learning professional cricket. These transformations are only possible because compassionate people chose to donate.Why your support is urgently neededProviding lifelong care for children with HIV, thalassemia and cancer requires constant support. There was even a time when Happy Feet Home had to shut its centre for nearly two weeks because of a lack of funding. During that period, children lost access to nutrition, education and mental health support. As Mansi explains, "Illnesses like HIV and Thalassemia are incurable. The need for medicine, for treatment, for care and support is going to be a forever need."That is why your donation matters today.Donate to Happy Feet HomeEvery donation helps provide medicines, nutritious meals, education, counselling and a loving home for children fighting serious illnesses. As Mansi beautifully puts it, "As a donor, you are not only giving money. You are ensuring that children with illnesses have the right to live as children. You are giving them hope."If you believe no child should be denied love, dignity or happiness because of illness, please support this NGO for children today. "If you believe that children with HIV, Thalassemia, Cancer have a right to live a dignified life please support our cause and donate today."Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Happy Feet Home in its mission to provide care, dignity, medical support, and hope to children living with life-limiting and life-shortening illnesses.

campaigns.title: Loving mother to 180 blind kids, visually impaired Veena needs your support in caring for them
campaigns.description: “A blind child is seen as a curse or as a burden to the family. These children are left on the street. I have picked up children from roadsides myself. I also lost my eyesight as a child but today I am a senior officer in a public sector company. What would I have done, had I not been taken care of?” asks Veena Mehta Verma who was once a beneficiary of National Association for the Blind, Delhi (NAB) and now works with the NGO to protect and care for blind children like herself.Today, hundreds of blind children supported by NAB, Delhi have found something that they never had before–hope for a better tomorrow. Without Veena and NAB, many of these children would be at the risk of going back to the streets or spend a life of neglect and even abuse. Your support to the NGO is crucial. Donate generouslyDonate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).A life of uncertainty and sufferingEven if a blind child is not abandoned they are often trapped in their homes deprived of education or any way of making a living. According to the nonprofit leader, “For a blind kid, employment is impossible without education. The (blind) kids need to learn Braille or they need ‘talking computer’ aids. Many of these kids are deprived of such facilities”.  Illuminating young lives “At NAB Delhi there are around 200-250 blind kids. There are around 180 kids in the hostel of NAB. We teach Braille, we teach arithmetic Taylor frames. To work towards a brighter future for the blind, we need your support. Please come forward and donate towards our mission”, says Veena. Students for whom NAB Delhi has cared for are today placed in some of the most prestigious organisations across the world. While some have gone on to make a name for themselves in the corporate world, others have taken up art and music as a profession too. Many blind children are bright, academically gifted, and waiting to shine, all they need is an opportunity. And your donation can give them just that.Donate to this fundraiser on Give.do, India’s largest and most trusted online donation platform, to help the blind children get shelter, education, care and a shot at a future full of opportunities.

campaigns.description: People of Assam need urgent help as floods leave lakhs in need. Donate nowFloodwaters have once again ravaged the beautiful land of Assam, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. According to the latest reports by the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), over 5.2 lakh people have been hit badly due to floods across Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sivasagar, and other districts. The number of victims of the natural disaster has climbed to 68 while thousands remain stranded without help. Together, let us rise and make a difference by contributing to our fundraising campaign for the flood victims of Assam.Charaideo is the worst-hit district with nearly 1.9 lakh people affected, followed by Sivasagar (over 1.5 lakh) and Jorhat (around 1.4 lakh). Nestled in the northeastern part of India, Assam has a long-standing history of facing nature's fury. Just last year, the state witnessed a devastating flood that uprooted the lives of countless individuals. This year, the floods have struck again, plunging numerous families into unimaginable chaos and distress. Many have been displaced from their homes, left without shelter, and robbed of their basic necessities.Embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure have also been damaged by flood waters. The urgent need for assistance:In times like these, it is our duty to extend a helping hand to our fellow human beings who are facing the wrath of nature. Your generous donations will directly support our on-ground NGO partners who are tirelessly working to provide immediate relief to the flood-affected people in Assam. The funds raised will be utilised to provide them with essential supplies such as food, clean water, and medical care, bringing hope and solace to their lives during this moment of crisis.The power of your donations:Every rupee contributed to this fundraising campaign will create a ripple effect of positive change in the lives of those who need it the most. Your support will help in:Immediate Relief: Ensuring that the affected families receive immediate assistance in the form of food, clean water, and essential supplies.Medical Care: Providing medical aid to those injured or suffering from waterborne diseases, ensuring their well-being in the aftermath of the disaster.Shelter and Rehabilitation: Assisting in the construction of temporary shelters and facilitating the process of rehabilitation to help affected families rebuild their lives.Here's how your donations can help:a) A food kit comprising essential supplies can be provided for ₹1,255. b) A hygiene kit with essentials for an entire family during floods can be ensured for ₹1,035. c) Our NGO partner can provide temporary shelter for flood-affected families for ₹2,570.Now is the time to unite and show our solidarity with the people of Assam. By donating to our fundraising campaign, you are not just providing immediate relief; you are also offering hope and strength to those who have lost everything. Together, we can make a difference and rebuild the lives of the flood-affected communities in Assam. Join us today and let compassion guide our actions.

campaigns.title: Help abandoned elderly with shelter and care
campaigns.description: Every day, elderly parents are left alone on the streets, at train stations, or even outside temples. Many are sick, struggling with age-related problems, and have no money or family to turn to. Some suffer for weeks or months before anyone notices their pain. The heartbreaking truth? They were abandoned by their own families.Although Indian law requires children and relatives to care for senior citizens, many elders still face neglect, abuse, and abandonment. The problem is only getting worse.But there is hope. Our dedicated NGO partners work day and night to rescue these forgotten elders. They provide safe shelter, medical care, nutritious meals, and most importantly—love and respect. Through old age homes across the country, our partners give these seniors a chance to live their remaining years with dignity, comfort, and peace.You can make a difference. Your donation will help our NGO partners:Rescue homeless elders from the streetsProvide shelter, food, and medical careRestore their faith in humanity with kindness and supportNo elder should spend their final years alone and suffering. Your generosity can give them a fresh start. Donate today and help an abandoned senior citizen find safety, care, and hope.
